_comment: Works as-is against the compose.yml in this repo - setup.sh writes the two values it needs (RCON_PASSWORD, BUILDER) into .env, and ${VAR} references here are resolved from the environment. Copy to rcon-servers.json only if you need more than one server or want to hand-edit. `access` decides who may drive the bot: "ops" (default) is anyone the server has opped, "everyone" is any player in chat, "allow" is only the listed names. RCON is console-level, so whoever may build may also clear a volume of someone's world - "everyone" is for worlds where you trust everyone who can join. `allow` is additive in every mode, which is how a non-OP gets access without being opped; with no ops.json and an empty allow list the bot refuses everybody. `operators` may remove other people's builds (defaults to the server's ops). `password` may be ${ENV_VAR}. `log` and the world dir are paths INSIDE the bot container - see compose.yml. ops.json is found beside the logs directory unless `ops` names it. `readVersion` is the minecraft-data registry used to read blueprints (see src/version.js).
